research_mode: official Home Office and ONS primary statistical publications only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel score, exact incident location, candidate value or business result

sources.name: CSEW strength and error
verified_claims: The CSEW is the most reliable indicator for long-term trends in common crime because it includes unreported crime and is unaffected by police activity or reporting-rate changes.
limitations: The survey remains subject to sampling error and non-sampling error such as recall problems.

sources.name: Police recorded crime limitations
verified_claims: Police recorded crime can show demand and policing effort, but for many crime types it is not a reliable measure of levels or trends and is not designated as accredited official statistics.
limitations: Recorded volumes can change because of reporting willingness, police activity and recording practice rather than underlying incidence alone.

sources.name: TACT release scope and revision
verified_claims: The 23 July 2026 TACT release covers Great Britain up to 31 March 2026 and combines accredited official statistics, official statistics and statistics in development.
limitations: Administrative case data are updated as cases progress, so figures can be revised.

sources.name: Terrorism-related arrests and context
verified_claims: There were 3,061 terrorism-related arrests in the year ending March 2026; 2,819 were linked to supporting Palestine Action after its proscription on 5 July 2025.
limitations: The exceptional event-specific component dominates the annual change and should not be used as a general local terrorism trend.

sources.name: Other terrorism-related arrests
verified_claims: Excluding arrests linked to supporting Palestine Action, there were 242 terrorism-related arrests, 44 of them in January to March 2026.
limitations: National arrest counts do not identify exposure or risk at a specific property.

sources.name: TACT charge outcomes
verified_claims: At the data-provision date, 551 of 3,061 arrests, or 18%, had resulted in a charge.
limitations: Many cases were unfinished, so charge counts and rates can increase in later releases.

sources.name: TACT arrests involving minors
verified_claims: There were 41 arrested individuals aged 17 or under; minors represented 17% of non-Palestine Action arrests where age was known.
limitations: Small national demographic counts must not be converted into local risk profiles.

sources.name: TACT court and custody totals
verified_claims: Seventy-two people were tried for terrorism-related offences in the year ending March 2026, and 273 people were in custody for terrorism or terrorism-connected offences at 31 March 2026.
limitations: Court and prison totals describe criminal-justice activity, not parcel-level public safety.

sources.name: TACT section 43 stop and search
verified_claims: The Metropolitan Police Service conducted 98 section 43 stops and searches and other England and Wales forces conducted 108; the latter series is published as Official Statistics in Development.
limitations: Stop-and-search counts are operational measures and the developing series requires cautious comparison.

sources.name: TACT principal offence rule
verified_claims: When a person is charged with multiple offences at the same time, the TACT statistics count only the most serious offence under the principal offence rule.
limitations: The resulting figures count people charged rather than every charge and must not be interpreted as total offence counts.
